turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. I'll do your blood pressure quickly before the doctor calls you. Sleeve up for me.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, fine. Make it quick, I'm wrecked and I've been waiting.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure is one forty-eight over ninety-two, heart rate 78. You here for the tummy, hey?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Tummy, and I can't sleep. I already told the lady at the desk.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Your file shows amlodipine, ten milligrams, once a day. Still taking that?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): No, ag, that's wrong. It's the blood pressure tablet, but I'm on five milligrams, not ten. They changed it last year sometime.
[SEG0007] person_1 (NURSE): I'll flag the mismatch for him. You can go in, he's free.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, one second, this thing has frozen again. Right. Howzit. What's been going on?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Stomach pain, and I'm not sleeping. Can we not start from zero, I just said it outside.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Shame, you look done in. Stomach pain, whereabouts? I only half caught the note.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Top of the stomach, under the ribs. Burning. About three weeks now. Worse after I eat, especially supper, and when I lie down it starts up.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, say that again? The screen just popped a warning. Three weeks, burning, after supper?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja. Three weeks. After supper, and lying down. Are you even listening?
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): I am, ja. Any vomiting?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No vomiting.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): And black stool, or blood when you go?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that. It's normal.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Okay. The sleep, tell me properly.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): I can't drop off, and then the burning wakes me at about two or three. Pretty much every night this last while. I'm useless on the road the next day.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Wakes you at two or three, sorry, come again? I clicked the wrong tab.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Two or three in the morning. Every night. Eish.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Are you taking anything for it? Painkillers, antacids, anything from the chemist?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Ibuprofen. Two tablets when the knee plays up, and lately I've been using it for this tummy as well. Doesn't do a thing for the burning.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): What strength, and how often? I didn't catch it.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): The box says 400 milligrams. Maybe one dose a day. Most days now.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Most days, or every day?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, I don't know. I forget some mornings. Three or four days in a week I miss it. Don't make me count, I'm tired.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any other tablets besides that and the blood pressure one?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Just those two.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sister flagged the amlodipine. File says ten milligrams. What do you actually take?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Five. Once in the morning. The ten is old, I told her.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alright, I won't guess a dose until we see the actual script. We'll leave it unclear.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke at all?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Never have. Can we move?
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): And drinking?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Socially.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Socially how? Weekends with friends?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, you know. It's not a whole thing. Braais, that sort of stuff.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Okay. Give me a moment, I'm opening the blood form and it's spinning.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): While you do that, the robot outside was out again this morning. Sat in the bakkie twenty minutes. Not your problem, hey.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): Load shedding's been hectic this side. Right, I'm back. Is the not sleeping only the pain, or do you lie there worrying as well?
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Mostly the pain. I have a glass of wine to try knock myself out. Which is dumb, I know.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): A glass. You said socially earlier. On a normal weeknight, how much wine are we talking?
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, a bottle of wine most nights, perhaps. Don't start, I'm irritable enough.
[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): No lecture from me. I appreciate you saying it straight. That amount can irritate the stomach, and I want to check your liver.
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): My working thought is gastritis, from the ibuprofen and the wine together. I can't fully rule out an ulcer.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Ulcer. Great. So what now, more waiting?
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm starting omeprazole, twenty milligrams by mouth, once every morning, half an hour before breakfast, for the acid. We'll do four weeks.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): And the ibuprofen?
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): Lay off it. It's hard on the stomach. If the knee needs something, use paracetamol instead.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): I've got paracetamol in the cupboard. Fine.
[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): Liver bloods today, and a full blood count with them. Sister will take them before you go.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): I skipped breakfast, the pain was bad. Does that mess the bloods up?
[SEG0054] person_3 (DOCTOR): Fasting is actually fine. Sorry, the pain was bad this morning on an empty stomach? Say again.
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja. It's worse when I haven't eaten as well, mornings too. I know I said after food, but it's both.
[SEG0056] person_3 (DOCTOR): Both, got it. Come back in two weeks for the results and to see if the omeprazole is helping. Sooner if you vomit blood, or the pain turns sudden and sharp.
[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks. If I can get off the bakkie runs. Those don't wait for a script.
[SEG0058] person_3 (DOCTOR): Book at reception on the way out. Cut the wine down if you can, even a little, take the omeprazole as I said, and no ibuprofen. The script will be at the front.
[SEG0059] person_1 (NURSE): I'll draw the bloods just now. Liver panel and the full blood count. Small scratch, then you're done.

Upper abdominal burning pain is also worse in the early morning/when fasting on an empty stomach; the patient clarified it is worse when he has not eaten as well, not only after food and lying down.
Insomnia detail not captured: the patient has trouble falling asleep, and the burning wakes him at about 2–3 AM every night.
Paracetamol was not only recommended; the patient said he already has paracetamol in the cupboard.
